name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI Management System

official_sources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 - Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system
Methodology: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 - AI - Guidance on risk management
NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

methodology: ISO/IEC 42001 requires an AI Management System (AIMS) following the harmonised high-level structure: Context (Clause 4), Leadership (5), Planning (6), Support (7), Operation (8), Performance Evaluation (9), Improvement (10). Annex A specifies 38 normative controls across nine objectives (A.2 AI Policy through A.10 Third Parties). Risk assessment follows ISO/IEC 23894 / ISO 31000: identify AI-specific risk sources, evaluate AI system impacts on individuals / groups / societies via AI system impact assessment, then treat through Annex A controls. Each control is attested against the organisation's AIMS scope (provider / producer / customer / partner / subject), implementation status, evidence, and a residual risk acceptance per the AI policy.

scoping_inputs.label: AI systems / models in scope of the AIMS
Training, validation and inference data sources
Intended AI use cases and deployment contexts

likelihood.label: Rare
likelihood.definition: May occur only in exceptional AI lifecycle conditions (<5%).

likelihood.label: Unlikely
likelihood.definition: Could occur but not expected during normal AI operation (5-25%).

likelihood.label: Possible
likelihood.definition: Might occur given the AI use case profile (25-50%).

likelihood.label: Likely
likelihood.definition: Will probably occur during normal AI lifecycle (50-75%).

likelihood.label: Almost Certain
likelihood.definition: Expected to occur given the AI use case (>75%).

impact.label: Insignificant
impact.definition: Negligible effect on individuals, groups, societies or organisational objectives.

impact.label: Minor
impact.definition: Limited adverse effect; recoverable; affects a small number of subjects.

impact.label: Moderate
impact.definition: Notable adverse effect; remediable; multiple subjects or one critical AI system.

impact.label: Major
impact.definition: Serious adverse effect on rights / freedoms / safety; large affected group; regulatory escalation likely.

impact.label: Severe
impact.definition: Widespread harm to fundamental rights, safety or society; AI system must be withdrawn or fundamentally re-engineered.

risk_model.calculation: likelihood * max(impact_c, impact_i, impact_a, impact_fairness, impact_safety)

controls.title: AI policy
controls.description: Document, communicate and review an AI policy reflecting the organisation's strategic intent, AI principles, and commitment to responsible AI.

questions.prompt: Implementation status of the AI policy?
Who owns the AI policy (e.g. Chief AI Officer, CISO)?
Evidence (policy document version, last review date, approval minutes).
How does the policy align with the organisation's wider risk and compliance frameworks?

controls.title: Alignment with other organisational policies
controls.description: Ensure the AI policy aligns with relevant policies (information security, privacy, quality, ethics).

questions.prompt: Which existing policies (ISMS, PIMS, ethics, HR) reference or are referenced by the AI policy?
Remediation plan if alignment gaps exist.

controls.title: AI roles and responsibilities
controls.description: Define, document and assign AI-related roles and responsibilities across the AI system lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Which AI roles are documented (AI owner, AI risk officer, model owner, data steward)?

controls.title: Reporting of concerns
controls.description: Establish a process for reporting AI-related concerns (whistleblowing, harm reporting, ethical concerns).

questions.prompt: How can internal and external parties report AI concerns?
Evidence: policy, reporting URL / hotline, recent reports handled.

controls.title: Resource documentation
controls.description: Identify and document the resources (data, tooling, computing, human) required across the AI system lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Training / validation / inference data sources and provenance documented?
Roles, competencies and human oversight capacity documented?

controls.title: AI system impact assessment process
controls.description: Establish a process to assess the potential impact of AI systems on individuals, groups of individuals and societies, throughout the AI system lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Which AI system is being assessed?
Who could be affected (individuals / vulnerable groups / society / environment)?
Impact on societies (democratic processes, environment, public safety)?
Existing safeguards (bias testing, human review, model cards).

controls.title: Documentation of AI system impact assessments
controls.description: Document the results of AI system impact assessments and retain them for the lifetime of the AI system.

questions.prompt: Number of AI systems with completed impact assessments.
Retention policy for impact assessment records.

controls.title: Responsible AI system design and development objectives
controls.description: Set objectives for the responsible design and development of AI systems addressing fairness, transparency, accountability, safety, security and privacy.

questions.prompt: Which responsible-AI objectives are formally set (e.g. fairness threshold, explainability target)?
How are objectives measured during design and development?
Evidence (design brief, model cards, bias-test reports).

controls.title: Verification and validation of AI systems
controls.description: Verify and validate AI systems against documented requirements throughout the lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Methods used (test datasets, adversarial testing, red-teaming, drift monitoring).

controls.title: Deployment of AI systems
controls.description: Document and apply controlled deployment of AI systems, including go/no-go criteria and post-deployment monitoring.

controls.title: AI system event logging
controls.description: Define, capture and retain AI system events sufficient for accountability, incident investigation and audit.

questions.prompt: Which events are logged (inputs, outputs, retraining, drift, human overrides)?

controls.title: Data for development and enhancement of AI systems
controls.description: Document data sources, acquisition methods, quality criteria and provenance for data used in AI development and operation.

questions.prompt: Is there a data inventory with provenance?
Lawful basis / consent records for personal data.

controls.title: Data quality for AI systems
controls.description: Establish and apply data-quality requirements appropriate to the AI system's intended use.

questions.prompt: Quality checks (drift detection, anomaly detection, representativeness tests).

domains.name: A.8 — Information for interested parties of AI systems

controls.title: System documentation and information for users
controls.description: Provide users with documentation enabling responsible use of the AI system (intended use, limitations, instructions, accuracy estimates).

questions.prompt: What user-facing documentation exists (system card, user guide, intended-use statement)?
Are model limitations explicitly disclosed to users?

controls.title: Communication of incidents
controls.description: Establish a process to communicate AI-related incidents to relevant interested parties (users, regulators, the public where required).

controls.title: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
controls.description: Define processes for the responsible use of AI systems, including intended-use boundaries and human oversight expectations.

questions.prompt: How are intended-use boundaries communicated and enforced?
Human oversight mechanism (human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, human review thresholds).

controls.title: Objectives for responsible use of AI systems
controls.description: Set and monitor objectives that ensure AI systems are used in line with their intended purpose.

questions.prompt: Objectives for responsible use (e.g. ban-list of prohibited uses, monitoring thresholds).
How is adherence to intended use monitored?

controls.title: Allocating responsibilities with third parties
controls.description: Document and allocate responsibilities between the organisation and third parties involved in the AI system lifecycle (data providers, model providers, integrators, customers).

questions.prompt: Which third parties are in scope (data providers, model providers, hosting, integrators)?
Contractual allocation of AI responsibilities, liability and audit rights.

controls.title: Customers
controls.description: Document how customer requirements concerning AI systems are identified and addressed.

questions.prompt: Process for capturing AI-specific customer requirements (transparency, bias, safety).
